reportOnlyUntil: Drew's review - no apply is authorized by this PR
finding: CF-A-JAPANESE-CARD-IS-NOT-AN-ENGLISH-CARD. The cell pokemon/2023 setKey `151` holds 715 catalog rows across three setNames, and 148 of them are JAPANESE cards ('2023 Pokemon Japanese Scarlet & Violet 151') sitting under a key the ruling sends to the ENGLISH tcgdex code sv03-5. The English 151 is sv03-5; the Japanese 151 is sv2a. This list routes those 148 rows to sv2a: 57 RETIRE where the Japanese twin already exists there, 91 RESLUG where the address is vacant. 0 collisions. The re-key lane's refusal guard could not stop the move because it compares PLAYER only and both markets print the SAME Pokemon at the SAME number -- 148 of 148 share a card number with an English row naming the same player, which is why report run 34061675440 said 0 REFUSED. The guard added in this PR refuses them by MARKET.
rulings: THE ENGLISH 151 AND THE JAPANESE 151 ARE DIFFERENT PRODUCTS, AND THE VOCABULARY ALREADY SAID SO. POKEMON_EN_SET_CODES maps sv03-5 -> '151' and POKEMON_JA_SET_CODES maps sv2a -> 'ポケモンカード151'. resolveSetKeyForSlug has drawn this line since #1900: hobbyIqCardId.service.ts:1817 tests the setName for /japanese/i and answers from the Japanese aliases BEFORE the English table is consulted, with the comment 'would otherwise hit the ENGLISH alias for 151 (sv03-5) and pool Japanese sales into the English card, which is a different print with a different market'. These 148 rows are what the catalog looks like where that rule was never applied.

sv2a IS THE DESTINATION AND IT IS A normalizeSetKey FIXED POINT, PINNED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. pokemonSetCodeIsTheKey.test.ts:184 asserts every emittable code (all 160 JA codes included) satisfies normalizeSetKey(c) === c, and pokemonEnglishSetKeyIsTheCode.test.ts:156 pins resolveSetKeyForSlug('pokemon','2023 Pokemon Japanese Scarlet & Violet 151',2023) === 'sv2a' -- the exact setName all 148 of these rows carry. The destination is the key the resolver would mint for them today.

sv2a ALREADY EXISTS FOR 2023 AND THE CHECKLIST TWIN WINS (CF-COUNT-BY-SOURCE-NOT-ROW-COUNT). Measured read-only: 1,381 rows at pokemon/2023/sv2a -- 420 from tcgdex-ja (2026-09-02 and 2026-09-04), the CHECKLIST authority for the Japanese product, plus 871 ingest-auto-seed-graded children and 90 ingest-auto-seed. Where a row's own destination slug is already occupied the incumbent wins and this row is a RETIRE, because a second row at one address is a split pool (CF-ONE-CARD-ONE-ROW-ONE-POOL). 57 entries are that case; 55 of those twins are ingest-auto-seed and 2 are tcgdex-ja.

A JAPANESE NAME IS NOT A DIFFERENT PLAYER. Two entries (#196 Erika's Invitation, #197 Giovanni's Charisma) point at destinations held by a tcgdex-ja row carrying the card's JAPANESE name -- エリカの招待 and サカキのカリスマ. Same number, same product, one card: a transliteration is not a collision, and the checklist row is the authority for the Japanese product, so both are RETIREs. NOTE FOR THE APPLY: relocate-catalog-rows-by-list compares playerName literally, so had these been listed as RESLUGs its occupied guard would have refused them -- correctly, on the information it has. They are listed as RETIREs, which takes no such comparison.

ALL 148 ARE ingest-auto-seed -- A DERIVED SOURCE, NEVER A TRANSCRIPTION. Not one of them is checklist-backed, so no checklist row is being retired or moved anywhere by this list. The 567 rows in the same cell that are NOT Japanese (398 'pokemon-tcg-data-scraped-2026-08-14' + 169 English-named ingest-auto-seed) are deliberately untouched: they are English cards and sv03-5 is their correct destination.

ORDER IS RETIRE-THEN-RESLUG AND THE LANE APPLIES IT TOP TO BOTTOM. No retire in this list vacates an address that a later reslug then claims -- the 57 retire destinations and the 91 reslug destinations are disjoint, and all 91 reslug destinations were point-read as VACANT -- but the order is stated explicitly because the lane does not reorder and a future edit to this file must not assume it will.

AN OCCUPIED ADDRESS IS STILL A COLLISION TO REPORT. All 91 reslug destinations were checked against the 1,381 live sv2a rows and every one is vacant, so this list expects 0 refusals. If the report run refuses any, the address was taken between the census and the run and that entry needs re-deciding -- never routing around.

THE POOL LIST IS EMPTY BECAUSE THE POOL IS EMPTY, MEASURED TWO WAYS. All 148 ids were counted in sold_comps by `cardId` AND by `hobbyiqCardId`: 0 and 0. No sales become unplaced by the 57 retires and none need re-pointing by the 91 reslugs. No pool list ships, because an empty file would misrepresent a measurement as an oversight.

THERE ARE NO GRADED CHILDREN UNDER 151 TO CARRY. The census projected gradeTier across all 715 rows in the cell: 0 graded rows. The 871 ingest-auto-seed-graded rows measured at sv2a are children of the sv2a parents, not of these.

census.method: read-only. One cross-partition query over card_catalog for sport='pokemon' AND (setKey='151' OR STARTSWITH(id,'hiq:pokemon:2023:151:')) projecting id/setKey/setName/playerName/cardNumber/year/source/parallel/gradeTier -- 715 rows, 158 RU. A second for sv2a (1,381 rows). Then, per JA row, an in-memory point check of its destination slug against those 1,381, and a sold_comps COUNT on all 148 ids by cardId and by hobbyiqCardId. No writes.
